subject: How to introduce a neighborhood matrix with incomplete spatial data through the years

messages.author: 9eeedbd24dc47df7
messages.subject: How to introduce a neighborhood matrix with incomplete spatial data through the years
parts:
Dear INLA members

I have gathered areal observations from systematic reviews and surveys for different areas through the years. I want to run a spatio-temporal analysis using INLA. I have read the LowBirthWeight example which introduces how I should formulate this model. In this example we have observation for all areas through the years. In my data set, I have observations just for some of these areas which I had a published study or survey for that year. So the observed number of areal units in the data set is smaller than  the total number of available areal units.

In LowBirthWeight example, the neighborhood matrix extracted from shapefile, and the data was sorted according to shapefile order through the years using following codes:

###Low Birth Weigth in Georgia (US)                                                        

data <- read.csv("data.final.csv")

georgia <- readShapePoly("co13_d00.shp")

data.georgia = attr(georgia, "data")

zzz <- poly2nb(georgia)

nb2INLA("Georgia.graph", zzz)

#this create a file called "LDN-INLA.adj" with the graph for INLA

Georgia.adj <- paste(getwd(),"/Georgia.graph",sep="")

#Order based on the map

order <- match(data.georgia$NAME,data[,1])

data<- data[order,]

#--Transform the data to be in the right format for INLA--#

low.vector <- as.vector(as.matrix(data[,2:12]))#by column

E.vector <- as.vector(as.matrix(data[,13:23]))#by column

year <- numeric(0)

for(i in 1:11){

  year<- append(year,rep(i,dim(data)[1]))

}

county<- as.factor(rep(data[,1],11))

 

data<- data.frame(y= low.vector, E= E.vector, ID.area=as.numeric(county), ID.area1=as.numeric(county), year=year,

                  ID.year = year, ID.year1=year, ID.area.year = #############################################################

formula.ST1<- y ~ 1 + f(ID.area,model="bym",graph=Georgia.adj) +

  f(ID.area1,year,model="rw1") + (year-mean(year))

model.inla.ST1 <- inla(formula.ST1,family="poisson",data=data,E=E, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

 

I am wondering whether it necessary to add new records for areas with missing information to create the same number of areal units for each year. On the other hand, whether the sparse spatial structure of data will mislead the model to distinguish correct neighborhood structure?

Kindest Regards,

Mahboubeh

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to introduce a neighborhood matrix with incomplete spatial data through the years
parts:
Hi

if you for some of the years, do not have a complete data or
observations in all regions, then either just skip these in the
data.frame or (if you want to do predictions), add them and set the
response to NA. you do not need to have complete observations.

Best
H
